Compute LIME-style Kernel Weights for Perturbations

Source: R/kumquat.R
kernel_weights.Rd

Weights each perturbation by its proximity to the point of interest using the exponential kernel from LIME, \(w = \sqrt{\exp(-d^2 / \sigma^2)}\), where \(d\) is the distance between the perturbation and the point of interest and \(\sigma\) is the kernel width.

Usage

kernel_weights(
  perturbations,
  poi,
  predictor_vars = names(poi),
  kernel_width = NULL,
  dist_fun = c("euclidean", "manhattan"),
  scale = TRUE
)

Arguments

perturbations

Data frame of perturbations

poi

a single row data.frame containing the point of interest

predictor_vars

Character vector of predictor variable names

kernel_width

Width of the exponential kernel. Defaults to 0.75 * sqrt(length(predictor_vars)), as in LIME.

dist_fun

Distance measure, one of "euclidean" or "manhattan"

scale

If TRUE (default), each predictor is divided by its standard deviation across the perturbations before computing distances, so the kernel width is independent of the perturbation radius.

Value

A numeric vector of weights, one per row of perturbations

Examples

poi <- data.frame(x = 1, y = 2)
perturbations <- generate_perturbations(
  poi,
  poi = poi,
  radius = 0.1,
  step = 0.05
)
kernel_weights(perturbations, poi, c("x", "y"))
#>  [1] 0.1814697 0.3441538 0.4259926 0.3441538 0.1814697 0.3441538 0.6526811
#>  [8] 0.8078868 0.6526811 0.3441538 0.4259926 0.8078868 1.0000000 0.8078868
#> [15] 0.4259926 0.3441538 0.6526811 0.8078868 0.6526811 0.3441538 0.1814697
#> [22] 0.3441538 0.4259926 0.3441538 0.1814697
